Description of the CAR
Compliance with existing environmental legislation is not ensured, as the relevant legislation is not evaluated
with RAMSAR areas found in eligible areas of the project.
Response from the project developer Date: 17-05-2021
The project was validated in 2016, complying with all current applicable regulations, while the Ramsar site of
the Bita River basin was declared in 2018. However, once the regulatory review and management plans were
carried out, it is found that the eligible areas of the project are compatible with the environmental legislation in
Colombia and with the regulations for the designation of areas of the Ramsar Convention. The areas
corresponding to the polygons of the Production or Commercial Forest Plantation Projects correspond to
multiple-use soils, following the Technical Guide for the Hydrographic Basin Ordering and Management Plans.
Documentation submitted by the project developer
Document with analysis of the legislation applicable to RAMSAR sites in Colombia.
Evaluation of the audit team Date: 23-05-2021
The project proponent has provided a document relevant to the evaluation of the legislation corresponding to
the Ramsar zones that are within the eligible areas of the project, giving clarity and feasibility to the areas.

Description of the CAR
The quality of the information and parameters used to quantify the reductions and / or removals of GHG
emissions is not assured will be provided in accordance with the methodology.
Since the calculation of the missing heights was done in a general way by joining species (the biology for each
species is different, including the responses in growth by site and by age), the technical and rigorous way to
perform this calculation is by regression. for each plot. Adjust this, as failure to do so can lead to over- or
underestimations.
Response from the project developer Date: 21-06-2021
Height predictions can be estimated by means of diameter-height models. If they are performed at the local level
considering the plantation lots, they increase their predictive capacity for the site. A local model can explain the
relationship between diameter and height regarding site condition, density, and management plan (López, Trincado,
Barrios, & Nieto, 2013). In addition, the project planted different species that must be considered independently to
ensure the quality of the analyses. The heights values were used to obtain two allometric models of heights (E. pellita
and E. tereticornis) as a function of DBH to estimate the total heights.
Documentation submitted by the project developer
A document in Excel format is attached and it has a lineal regression by specie. According to every regression,
a model of height as a function of DBH is described to estimate the total heights.
210618_Ecuacion_Alometrica_Altura
Evaluation of the audit team Date: 29-06-2021
The project proponent describes the methodology of how he estimates the heights for the project species.

CCB & VCS VERIFICATION REPORT:
CCB Version 3, VCS Version 3
CCB v3.0, VCS v3.4 44
The project requirements are not ensured in terms of data and parameters corresponding to the quality of the
information and it is necessary to justify in greater detail within the Risk of Non-Permanence the procedures to
consider the uncertainty.
Since this is the first time that inventory data and carbon calculation are presented for the Anacardium
occidentale species, this is a species that, due to biology and management, looks for fruits and not wood, which
represents a significant adjustment in the calculation of biomass. and therefore, of carbon. Given this high level
of uncertainty and while having more adjusted equations, in this condition it is recommended to increase or
report higher levels of discount for risk. Coincidentally, the permanence analysis tool punishes this species more
than the others, so it is suggested to include this condition in the discount justifications.
Response from the project developer Date: 21-06-2021
The Cashew (Anarcardium occidentale) is widely recognized by its high potential in production of nut to
international market demand (Sindoni Vielma, Hidalgo Loggiodice, & Méndez Natera, 2009). The Cashew trunk
is used for furniture construction; the bark is used to make inks; the fruit is used in the production of sweets,
preserves, wines and the nut is used to harden chocolates and to make sweets and juices (Lafont, Páez, &
Portacio, 2011). According to the above-mentioned uses, allometric equation to estimate total volume or total
biomass for Cashew tree are few. One of these was the study conducted by Biah et al (2018) to assess the
carbon sequestration potential of Anacardium occidentale and which derived the equation used for project. For
this reason, the Risk Rating in the Project management section of the Non-Permanent Risk consider the highest
value.
Documentation submitted by the project developer
The justification was included in the Canapro Non-Permanent Risk, and it was clarified on the monitoring report
in section 3.2.2
210618_VCS-Non-Permanence-Risk-Report_Vichada_CP_ENG
Evaluation of the audit team Date: 29-06-2021
The project proponent makes the modifications in the non-permanence risk document and makes the
modification in the monitoring report.
CAR Closed

Law 1753 of 2015, in article 175, orders the creation of the National Registry for the Reduction of GHG Emissions
and resolution 1447 of 2018 regulates the Monitoring, Reporting and Verification system of mitigation actions at
the national level. This resolution regulates the registration on the RENARE platform of all mitigation initiatives
developed in the country and the accounting for each project. In resolution 0831, which modifies resolution 1447
of 2018, it is mentioned that on the RENARE platform, only results of Greenhouse Gases mitigation with a
validity of no more than five years can be reported and canceled. However, it does not mention the distinction
in the project documents of the possible markets where the mitigation results could be traded or canceled.
To comply with this regulation, the grouped project for commercial forest plantations initiatives in the department
of Vichada is registered on the RENARE platform in its feasibility and formulation phases and is currently in the
implementation phase.
Once the project is verified and the mitigation results are issued, the accounting information will be updated in
the implementation phase in accordance with the standard.
Documentation submitted by the project developer
Support documentation of registration of the grouped project for commercial forest plantations initiatives in the
department of Vichada by the RENARE platform.
Evaluation of the audit team Date: 23-05-2021
The project proponent presents the initiative status report on the RENARE platform.

Description of the CL
Compliance with current environmental legislation is not ensured since the necessary calculations of water
rounds or bodies of water are not made to identify the eligible areas of the project.
Response from the project developer Date: 17-05-2021
The spatial information acquired for the eligibility process comes from the Landsat TM and ETM+ sensors in the
years 2001 and 2011 with a spatial resolution of 30m that represents a scale of the cartographic product
1:100,000 and a planimetric precision (greater than 90%) on objects with distances greater than 50m on the
ground, therefore, although in the eligibility process, the eligible, ineligible and water classes are identified, by
scale, the edge effect of the pixels of the water class on eligibility occurs on the ground over distances greater
than 50 meters, therefore, compliance with the 30-meter distance is guaranteed, even if the eligible area is lost.
The eligibility product is not comparable with a satellite image of better spatial resolution such as those used by
the GeoEye sensor of the Google Earth platform with a spatial resolution of 1 m, because an eligibility that was
made on a scale of 1: 100,000 would be compared with an Image that gives details of the elements on the
ground at a scale of 1: 3,000, where the elements detected in the form of eligibility will not be the same as those
detailed with another source of information.
Documentation submitted by the project developer
Evaluation of the audit team Date: 23-05-2021
The project proponent clarifies the differences that arise when identifying the eligible areas of the project,
considering the scales that are handled according to the platforms and / or satellite images used to identify the
water rounds and bodies of water, and thus perform the procedures required for the eligible areas of the project.
CL Closed
